entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Taylor & Francis, a distinguished commercial publishing group, was founded in 1852 in London, England, and has since become a pivotal player in academic publishing. This institution is headquartered in Milton Park, Oxfordshire, and primarily focuses on disseminating scholarly research across a multitude of disciplines, encompassing the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. The group has played a significant role in advancing academic communication and knowledge sharing, particularly during the rise of modern scholarship in the late 19th and 20th centuries.

The company gained prominence through the publication of various influential journals and books, collaborating with esteemed scholars and institutions to produce high-quality academic content. By the early 20th century, Taylor & Francis had established itself as a key player in the academic publishing landscape, launching notable titles such as the "International Journal of Epidemiology" and the "Journal of Behavioral Medicine." The company has continued to innovate, adapting to the digital age by offering online access to its extensive library of journals and books, thereby broadening the reach of academic research to a global audience.

The legacy of Taylor & Francis is evident in the way it has transformed scholarly communication. By fostering an environment where research can be readily accessed and disseminated, the group has influenced policy-making, education, and scientific discourse worldwide. The impact of their publications can be seen in the citations and academic discussions that continue to reference their works, thereby ensuring that their contributions to knowledge remain relevant and impactful.
